speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: In New Mexico, if you walk home alone at night,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: and black wool is lying at the crossroads... don't cross it.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Because that isn't wool. And it only waits for people who are alone.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: They call her La Mala Hora. The Evil Hour.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: In 1910, a folklorist recording Spanish folklore in New Mexico wrote about her.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: He described a spirit that haunts dark crossroads,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: terrorizing people who walk alone at night.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Most of the time, it looks like a lock of wool.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Sometimes, a whole sheep's fleece.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: According to the legend, she can also become a woman in black.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: But here's the terrifying part.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: She isn't there for you.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: They say if you see her at the crossroads,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: someone you love will die soon.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: She doesn't chase you. She doesn't make a sound.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: She just watches you walk home... to see which door you open.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: So if you're ever on a dark New Mexico road tonight,

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: don't cross alone.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Because that wool isn't lying in the road by accident.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: It's waiting to see who you'll lose.
